value.emollient_frequency: once daily as normally used, applied at least 3 hours after application of investigational product, to untreated areas only
prohibited_concomitant: Systemic antifungal agents, corticosteroids, immunosuppressive therapies, retinoids, roflumilast, or apremilast (Otezla) -- 4-week washout before Baseline
Topical antifungals, corticosteroids, calcineurin inhibitors, sulfur-based treatments, medical devices, crisaborole (Eucrisa), azelaic acid, or metronidazole -- 2-week washout before Baseline

Medicated shampoos (eg, coal tar, keratolytics including salicylic acid, antifungals, zinc pyrithione, selenium sulfide, corticosteroids, medical devices) -- 2-week washout before Baseline, and prohibited during the study
Topical medications used on the scalp for conditions besides seborrheic dermatitis (eg, topical minoxidil for androgenetic alopecia) -- 4-week washout before Baseline
Phototherapy, tanning beds, other light-emitting devices -- 4-week washout before Baseline
Investigational drugs -- 12 weeks (biologics) or 5 half-lives, whichever longer; 5 half-lives (orals); 2 weeks (topical)
permitted_concomitant: Eye drop and nasal corticosteroid preparations are allowed
Inhaled corticosteroid preparations are allowed if used for a stable condition at a stable dose for >28 days before screening and continued at the same dose throughout the study
Non-medicated emollients, moisturizers, and sunscreens once daily as normally used, applied at least 3 hours after investigational product, to untreated areas only
Chronically used medications (particularly statins and anti-hypertensives) are allowed unless separately prohibited in Table 1
Only non-medicated shampoos are permitted; subjects should not use other hair products for at least 1 hour before or after application of investigational product
value.population_note: This is a monotherapy design (ARQ-154/roflumilast foam 0.3% QD vs vehicle foam QD, applied to all affected areas for the full 8-week treatment period) with a formal prohibited/permitted concomitant medication table (Table 1) rather than a standardized background topical regimen -- there is no background TCS or co-administered active agent.

background_therapy.source_excerpt: 4.5.1 Prohibitions and Concomitant Therapy: Prohibited medications and products are detailed in Table 1... Note: Eye drop and nasal corticosteroid preparations are allowed. Inhaled corticosteroid preparations are allowed if used for a stable condition and at a stable dose for > 28 days before screening and are continued at the same dose throughout the study. Non-medicated emollients, moisturizers and sunscreens will be allowed once daily as normally used by the subjects and applied at least 3 hours after application of randomized investigational product to untreated areas only... Only non-medicated shampoos are permitted. Medicated shampoos ... are prohibited.

study_schedule.source_excerpt: Duration of Participation for Subjects: Screening (up to 4 weeks) + Treatment phase (8 weeks) and follow-up (1 week post-treatment completion) for a total of up to approximately 13 weeks. ... Study Design: This is a parallel group, double blind, vehicle-controlled study in which ARQ-154 foam 0.3% or vehicle foam is applied QD x 8 weeks to adult subjects with at least moderate seborrheic dermatitis affecting the scalp and/or rest of body. 1.2 Study Schema: Screening (Visit 1) -> Baseline (Visit 2) Randomization and Treatment Day 0 -> 8-Week Treatment Period (Visits 3, 4, & 5) -> Follow Up Period / Visit 6.
